question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? In 1862, the Scottish physicist James Clerk Maxwell put forward the idea that light needs an ether in order to travel. This theory ______ to account for the nature of light, though embraced for a while, ultimately fell out of favor within the scientific community.
option a: attempts
option b: was attempting
option c: attempting
option d: attempted
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The non-finite participle 'attempting' modifies the subject without adding a second finite verb alongside 'fell out of favor.'

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? In his experimental film Koyaanisqatsi (1982), Godfrey Reggio adjusts his footage to match Philip Glass's original score, applying slow motion to some shots of commuters and time-lapse to others and rhythmically cutting between flowing water and streaming automobile traffic, among other pairings, so as to produce ______ images and music.
option a: a hierarchy among
option b: a consonance between
option c: an exaggeration of
option d: a mystery from
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'A consonance between' captures the harmony Reggio creates by pairing image with music.

question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text? Claudine Mukesharugo grows tea in Rwanda and Vinicio Gonzales grows coffee in Guatemala; both belong to a worldwide network of smallholder farmers who work with the grassroots group Thrive Farmers. That collaboration rests on a revenue-sharing arrangement designed to keep farmers front and center: instead of merely supplying raw crops, the farmers hold a stake in the sale of the finished products.
option a: To explain that certain small farmers follow a business model that gives them a larger role in selling the products made from their crops
option b: To describe how a partnership between two farms growing different crops produced a new business model for small farmers
option c: To introduce the claim that small farmers around the world are increasingly running their farms as if they were large businesses
option d: To suggest that the Thrive Farmers organization is creating stronger global demand for crops grown by small farmers
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The central point is that some small farmers use a model letting them share in selling the finished products made from their crops.

question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text? In Nimipuutimt, an Indigenous language of the interior Northwest of what is now the United States, the word pit'iin' means 'girl,' while pi-pit'in' refers to two or more girls. When a piece of a root word reappears, sometimes altered, inside a related word, the process is known as reduplication; here the 'pi' of pit'iin' recurs in pi-pit'in'. Nimipuutimt contains many instances of this kind of reduplication.
option a: It describes how Nimipuutimt relates to several other languages, poses a question about that relationship, and then answers the question.
option b: It names the most common words in Nimipuutimt, explains why translating them into English is difficult, and then lists other languages into which they can be translated.
option c: It explains reduplication, notes why the phenomenon has been controversial among scholars, and then argues that studying Nimipuutimt could settle that controversy.
option d: It presents some particular words in Nimipuutimt, describes the general linguistic phenomenon those words illustrate, and then states that this phenomenon is common in the language.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The text gives sample words, defines the phenomenon (reduplication) they illustrate, and states it occurs often in Nimipuutimt.

question: Which choice most logically completes the text? In 2013, Shirley Ann Williams and colleagues carried out a meta-analysis (a review of earlier research) of studies on the social media site once called Twitter, among them Brody and Diakopoulos's 2011 paper 'Cooooooooooooooollllllllllllll!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Using Word Lengthening to Detect Sentiment in Microblogs,' in order to spot research trends. The team found that although a substantial number of papers examined user profiles, many others examined message content. They further noticed that studies focused on message content were especially prone to rely on knowledge discovery methods (techniques from statistical analysis and artificial intelligence built to handle enormous quantities of data), implying that ______
option a: researchers tended to expect the quantity of information contained in social media messages to be unusually large.
option b: studies employing knowledge discovery methods are cited more widely than studies that do not.
option c: researchers generally assumed that a small share of users accounts for most of the information in social media messages.
option d: knowledge discovery methods produce less reliable results when applied to user profiles than to message content.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Using big-data methods on message content implies researchers expected that content to hold especially large amounts of information.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? Science fiction has long acted as a ______ real-world technological progress. Indeed, from Jules Verne's 1865 novel From the Earth to the Moon inspiring advances in aerospace engineering to the television show Star Trek prompting the design of the forerunner of today's smartphones, such stories have driven many genuine innovations.
option a: diversion from
option b: constraint to
option c: catalyst of
option d: sponsor of
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Catalyst of' fits, since the examples show science fiction spurring actual technological advances.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? Dinosaur exhibits at institutions like Chicago's Field Museum of Natural History (whose collection includes a mounted Apatosaurus skeleton) stand out for the ______ of the research supporting them--staff drew on numerous sources to ensure the displays were accurate.
option a: rigor
option b: obscurity
option c: shallowness
option d: novelty
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Rigor' matches the thorough, source-checked research described.

question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the researcher's claim? A group of public transit specialists in Buffalo is planning a new light rail stop on the Buffalo Metro Rail to serve a neighborhood that currently has no stop. To choose the location, the team relies on a survey from ten years ago that asked residents how far they would be willing to walk to a light rail stop. The team also reviewed research showing that willingness to walk to transit is shaped by factors such as weather and the presence of well-enforced low speed limits for cars. One researcher contends that the survey no longer reflects how the neighborhood's present-day residents feel.
option a: Buffalo residents are far less likely to ride public transit on rainy days than on clear days.
option b: People who currently ride the Buffalo Metro Rail are content with the number of stops on the line.
option c: Over the past ten years there has been a sharp rise in cyclists using the roads in the neighborhood the new stop will serve.
option d: Enforcement of posted speed limits in the neighborhood the new stop will serve has increased substantially over the past ten years.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: If enforcement of speed limits (a factor affecting willingness to walk) changed markedly over ten years, the old survey may no longer capture current residents' feelings.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Many writings by the Roman engineer Frontinus (1st century CE) are ______ his De aquaeductu, an account of the Roman aqueduct system, is an extant work: it can still be read today.
option a: lost, and conversely
option b: lost. Conversely,
option c: lost and conversely,
option d: lost, conversely,
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A period after 'lost' correctly separates the two independent clauses, with 'Conversely,' opening the second.

question: As used in the text, what does the word "considered" most nearly mean? The passage below is from Chinua Achebe's 1964 novel Arrow of God, set in Nigeria during the 1920s. Ezeulu, the religious leader of several villages, declares when the yearly yam harvest may begin. Whenever Ezeulu considered the immensity of his power over the year and the crops and, therefore, over the people he wondered if it was real. It was true he named the day for the feast of the Pumpkin Leaves and for the New Yam feast; but he did not choose it. He was merely a watchman. His power was no more than the power of a child over a goat that was said to be his. (c)1964 by Chinua Achebe
option a: Anticipated
option b: Respected
option c: Allowed
option d: Pondered
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Here 'considered' means reflected on or pondered the extent of his power.

question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole? The following is from Yung Wing's 1909 memoir My Life in China and America. Yung Wing was the first person from China to graduate from a US university. Little did I realize when in 1845 I wrote, while in the Morrison School, a composition on "An Imaginary Voyage to New York and up the Hudson," that I was to see New York in reality. This incident leads me to the reflection that sometimes our imagination foreshadows what lies uppermost in our minds and brings possibilities within the sphere of realities.
option a: It illustrates the sense of adventure that Yung developed as a child.
option b: It recounts an event in Yung's life that exemplifies a phenomenon.
option c: It shows Yung's childhood unwillingness to distinguish between reality and fantasy.
option d: It foreshadows the difficulties Yung would later face in publishing his writings.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The underlined sentence treats Yung's boyhood essay as an instance of imagination foreshadowing reality.

question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text? Creating protected areas (PAs), such as Fiji's Mamanuca Islands, is a widespread conservation approach, yet because PAs limit certain economic activities, many assume they slow economic development. Part of what fuels this assumption is that economic assessments frequently overlook the indirect effects of tourism linked to PAs. Anubhab Gupta and colleagues, however, found that tourism tied to the Mamanuca Islands raises local demand for goods and services in other sectors, resulting, for example, in higher income from livestock production in nearby areas.
option a: It generalizes about the difficulty of using PAs to reconcile economic and conservation aims, shows why most PAs fail to meet that aim, and then offers one PA as proof the aim is achievable.
option b: It presents a widely held belief about how PAs affect the economy, suggests why that belief is so widespread, and then describes a study whose findings appear to contradict it.
option c: It states a hypothesis for why PAs generally harm local economies, shows how one team's findings support it, and then explains how another team's new method led to a different conclusion.
option d: It describes how PAs typically affect economic development where they are established, summarizes several supporting economic studies, and then concedes that one PA is an exception to the trend.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The text states a common belief about PAs, explains its prevalence, then cites a study whose findings seem to contradict it.

question: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Nunez and colleagues' claim? Rafael Nunez and colleagues examined how the Yupno, an Indigenous people of Papua New Guinea, conceive of time in both speech and gesture. The researchers filmed Yupno speakers explaining certain temporal words and phrases, such as abjuk, a present-oriented expression meaning "now," and coded the hand gestures each speaker made. Earlier work has shown that many cultures mark temporal distinctions along imagined straight-line axes; English speakers, for instance, often use a front/back axis to place events in time. Some scholars hold that this tendency is universal, but Nunez and colleagues argue that it is not.
option a: Yupno speakers typically use their left hand to make temporal gestures, whether the gestures refer to the past or to the future.
option b: Some Yupno grammatical structures used to talk about time also appear in English.
option c: Yupno speakers were observed making temporal gestures both indoors and outdoors, though more frequently indoors.
option d: Future-oriented gestures used by Yupno speakers do not, on average, point in the opposite linear direction from past-oriented ones.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: If future and past gestures don't fall along opposite directions of a line, the Yupno aren't mapping time onto a linear axis, supporting the claim that the tendency isn't universal.

question: Based on the information in the text and table, is the tour guide's claim supported? Percent Change in Stopover Visits from Canada (2024 to 2025). Table columns: Location, Q1 2024, Q1 2025, Change (%). Anguilla: 720, 773, 7.4. Cayman Islands: 11,409, 12,374, 8.5. Cuba: 399,254, 272,274, -31.8. Curacao: 15,716, 17,941, 14.2. Mexico: 784,150, 822,538, 4.9. In tourism, a "stopover" means spending at least one night in a place while en route to another destination, whether for personal or business travel. A tour guide comes across a table recording Canadians' stopover visits during January-March (Q1) of 2024 and of 2025. The guide claims that, among the listed locations, Cuba had the largest drop in such visits by people traveling for personal reasons yet remained a very popular stop in both periods.
option a: No, because even though the table shows Cuba had high numbers of stopover visits from Canada in both periods, that total was several hundred thousand lower than Mexico's peak in those periods
option b: No, because even though the table shows Cuba had more total stopover visits from Canada than most other locations did in both periods, it doesn't show the numbers by type of travel
option c: Yes, because the table shows Cuba had the second highest total number of stopover visits from Canada in both Q1 2024 and Q1 2025
option d: Yes, because the table shows the percent change in stopover visits from Canada to Cuba between the two periods was negative, indicating a decline in totals for both types of travel
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The table gives only totals, not a breakdown by personal vs. business travel, so the claim about personal-travel visits isn't supported.

question: The information in the text and the graph best supports which conclusion about the data sets used in Wang et al.'s study? (Graph titled "Correlations Between Length-of-Season Estimates from GPP and SIF Data Sets"; y-axis "Correlation" ranging from -0.1 to 0.9; x-axis groups FLUXNET, FLUXCOM, RF-GPP; bars for SIF data set A, SIF data set D, SIF data set F.) Gross primary productivity (GPP), the rate at which plants fix carbon during photosynthesis, is usually inferred from carbon flux observations. Because the onset and cessation of photosynthesis track with the seasons and GPP shifts accordingly, GPP data sets built from carbon flux observations, including FLUXNET, FLUXCOM, and RF-GPP, can be used to estimate the length of the growing season. Investigating whether another proxy for photosynthesis--solar-induced chlorophyll fluorescence (SIF), solar radiation re-emitted by plants and detectable via satellite--could gauge growing-season length, Zhe Wang et al. computed correlations between estimates from several SIF data sets (a sample of which appear in the graph) and estimates from GPP data sets (values nearer 0 indicate weaker correlations).
option a: The weaker correlations between SIF data set F and all three GPP data sets, relative to those of the other SIF data sets, suggest that data set F systematically underestimates the length of the growing season.
option b: Because the range between the highest and lowest FLUXCOM values is greater than FLUXNET's more limited range, FLUXCOM-derived estimates of growing-season length vary more widely than FLUXNET-derived estimates do.
option c: Length-of-season estimates derived from RF-GPP data were generally more similar to those derived from FLUXCOM data than to those derived from FLUXNET data.
option d: The stronger correlations between all three SIF data sets and the FLUXCOM and RF-GPP data sets, relative to those between all three SIF data sets and FLUXNET, suggest that FLUXCOM and RF-GPP enable more accurate estimates of growing-season length than FLUXNET does.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Across the SIF data sets, correlations with RF-GPP track more closely with FLUXCOM than with FLUXNET.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? To grasp what scholars regard as the allegorical intent of Botticelli's 15th-century painting ______ to embody the virtues of love, peace, and purity--a viewer must become familiar with the painting's symbolic elements.
option a: The Birth of Venus, namely
option b: The Birth of Venus, namely--
option c: The Birth of Venus, namely,
option d: The Birth of Venus--namely,
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A dash before 'namely,' frames the parenthetical aside and matches the closing dash before 'a viewer.'

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? In the 4th century BCE, the ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle argued that objects move only when it is in their nature to do so. This theory ______ to explain the fundamental principles of motion, though embraced for a time, eventually fell out of favor within the scientific community.
option a: attempts
option b: was attempting
option c: attempted
option d: attempting
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The participle 'attempting' modifies the subject without creating a second finite verb alongside 'fell out of favor.'

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? Yuen Yuen Ang et al. contend that simply counting how many patents are filed each year ______ how much innovation is actually taking place: genuinely novel patents--those, like a 2011 patent for an automated navigation system for planes, that unite previously unconnected technological domains--are vastly outnumbered by nonnovel ones (for instance, a 2008 patent for a method of making soup).
option a: belies
option b: portends
option c: thwarts
option d: maligns
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Belies' fits: the raw patent count misrepresents the true, much smaller degree of real innovation.

question: Which choice best states the function of the underlined sentence? Magical realism, a style that threads fantasy through otherwise realistic stories, took shape in Latin America during the 1960s. It is closely tied to Gabriel Garcia Marquez, whose One Hundred Years of Solitude is a defining text. Mexican American writers took up the style as well, such as Ana Castillo, who drew on Mexican folktales as a source of fantasy in So Far from God. Yet The Mixquiahuala Letters, also by Castillo, contains no fantastical plot events. And despite his popular reputation, Garcia Marquez himself wrote several works of strict realism, including Chronicle of a Death Foretold.
option a: To identify an unnoticed point of similarity between Chronicle of a Death Foretold and So Far from God
option b: To suggest that Mexican American authors influenced by Garcia Marquez may, in turn, have influenced him
option c: To counter the possible impression that Garcia Marquez wrote in the magical realist style in all of his works
option d: To dispute the common assumption that One Hundred Years of Solitude is superior to Garcia Marquez's realist works
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The sentence corrects the potential assumption that Garcia Marquez always wrote magical realism by noting his strictly realist works.

question: What does the text most directly suggest about translation apps? The linguist John McWhorter maintains that translation apps for smartphones and computers--though they generally miss many subtleties--are steadily reducing the need to learn new languages. Improvements in language-processing technology have sharply increased these apps' usefulness for routine tasks, such as asking about a menu item, and for brief encounters; even so, richer communication (say, in business dealings or meaningful personal exchanges) often depends on conversational patterns and fine gradations of meaning.
option a: They have improved remarkably over time but remain insufficient to support the complexity called for in certain interactions.
option b: They are coming to be embraced by international tourists but are viewed with skepticism by many business professionals.
option c: They are becoming simpler to use but are inconsistent in how comprehensively they cover different languages.
option d: They have gained impressive capabilities but continue to be widely viewed as inadequate for most practical purposes.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The text says the apps have improved greatly yet still cannot handle the nuance that richer interactions require.
